added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no base gate log, so the added-failure count was not taken

findings.text: the test named as the guard on the carried list asserts membership in the same tuple it reads and names four of the five entries, omitting RECKON_RUN_STORE, while the dispatch case asserts only RECKON_HOME of the five in the spec, so dropping any of the other four names from _carried_crew_environment() or from the spec write leaves the gate green.

item_verdicts.diff: read against base 7cc73727 as one commit of five files, +686/-2: the spec's environment mapping with the carried-name constant in reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6275-6355, the overlay with its refusals in reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:603-661, the bounded survival confirm at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6325, the new test file, and the fragment with its before/after figure.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when is the three named files passing with the real spawn verb under a crew home other than the batch step's, and the dispatch case failing under the declared mutation; the gate log records 26 passed, exit 0, the red log records 1 failed in 6.04s, and my own re-run of that case at the reviewed head passed in 6.43s.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is the dispatcher's crew environment travelling to the per-run supervisor and dispatch failing when that supervisor has exited within its first seconds; reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6292 carries the five crew-state names and reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6634 confirms the supervisor survived on both the fleet and fork branches.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it names commit 3d39976f, the gate command with 26 passed, exit 0, the test and negative-control logs on disk, and its landing line as the plan comment prose; its baseline_suite and after_suite fields are prose, so neither gate log resolves from them.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared paths are the two production modules, the new test file, the fragment and the figure directory; git show --stat 3d39976f lists exactly those five paths and nothing else.

justifications.durability: the reinstated regression (spawn_supervisor starting argv with dict(environ)) reddens the dispatch case, so the RECKON_HOME carry is genuinely guarded, but tests/test_fleet_lane_carries_the_dispatch_environment.py:330 asserts membership in the very tuple it reads and omits RECKON_RUN_STORE, leaving the other four names and the set-only-when-present rule unguarded.
justifications.evidence: the recorded gate is a real one (gate-after.log: revision 7cc73727, 26 passed, exit 0) and the negative control reddens exactly the intended case (CrewError "exited within 2s of starting: worker did not spawn: CrewError: no live run", 1 failed in 6.04s), but the manifest's suite fields are prose, so added_failure_count reads unmeasured (null) rather than a measured zero.
justifications.fit: the change follows the module's idiom, a named module constant with a per-name comment at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6270, refusal rather than coercion at the spec boundary at reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:603, and a bounded wait built on the existing branch structure at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6634, and its new source carries no plan, sprint or ticket label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: both halves land at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6292, which selects the five crew-state names, and reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6658 and :6669, which confirm the supervisor survived on the fleet and fork branches, with the gated case showing a supervisor reaching a run under a crew home other than the batch step's.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat 3d39976f lists exactly the five declared write paths, so the diff stays inside its fence and carries nothing the goal does not imply.
